correctness.rationale: The concept class uses distinct unordered pairs of lines, not unions, an incidence difference over F3, or the binary span of all line vectors. Every pair gives weight 6, and a collision would give a nonzero binary dependency on at most four lines. The line-incidence kernel is generated by the sum of all 13 lines (also follows from the rank of the binary Gram matrix I+J). I reconstructed the lines as spans of pairs of projective points and the projective group from elementary coordinate generators. All 8,192 restrictions give shattering counts (1,13,78,286,702) in degrees 0 through 4 and zero thereafter; all 702 facets have cardinality four. For k=4 the orbit sizes are 13,468,234 with respectively a full line, precisely one collinear triple and no collinear triple; for k=5 they are 117,702,468 in the order stated. A full projective line cannot be all positive: when selected it loses the one intersection point, and when not selected it meets the summands in at most two positive points. The two non-line four-orbits have all traces and the stated absent five-traces check exactly. Every smaller support extends to a non-line four-set; every larger shattered set would have a shattered five-subset. For depth five all 32 leaves in the supplied tree have valid, distinct hypotheses, starting at root query 0, with the left/right encoding as stated. Pair-transitivity gives 78*6/13=36 positives at one point and 78*choose(6,2)/choose(13,2)=15 positives jointly at distinct points. Below the positive root answer a depth-six tree would need at least 16 distinct hypotheses for each answer to the second query. A distinct point gives only 15 for the positive answer, and repeating the root gives none for the negative answer. An independent recursive split calculation also finds depth five and excludes six. These conclusions establish both dimensions and purity only for the specified finite class.

value.rationale: This is the first odd-order projective plane and its natural fixed two-line parity layer, not an arbitrary subgroup or sample. A geometric obstruction law describing every static support is more useful than just a scalar dimension; purity and the two distinct facet geometries provide a concrete comparison with related projective union/coding families. The strict 4-versus-5 gap and the simple local incidence proof of the online ceiling show what adaptive queries add in this exact incidence geometry. No claim beyond the enumerated plane is needed for that comparison to be useful.
